gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2's '1,000 W solar' comes through a single input capped at 20 A under a 60 V ceiling, so the panel string must run at 50 V or more to reach 1,000 W, while each of the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus's two 15 A inputs reaches its 500 W cap from about 33.3 V upward.
standout_why: I compared this against Volt & Valley's combo page (cited in both chats) and StormWatts (rank 4 in the pinned chat). I also checked the shopper's live search for the same query, which brought up a Walmart ABOK listing and pages from Dabbsson, Pecron and Jackery. Volt & Valley gives the DELTA 3 Plus as '2 MPPT inputs of 500W each' and publishes no voltage or current for any station. It does not cover the Elite 100 V2. StormWatts gives the DELTA 3 Plus per-port limits (11–60 V, 15 A, 500 W each) and checks cold Voc against 60 V. It does not work out what operating voltage the panels need to reach the rated watts, and it does not cover the Elite 100 V2. ChatGPT's plain chat called the Elite 100 V2 'another option' with 1,000 W on one input, but nothing it got compares the two 1,000 W ratings on the same basis.
decides: This confirms the DELTA 3 Plus as the pick. Its 1,000 W comes from two 500 W inputs, and an ordinary 400–500 W string on each input reaches the cap with room to spare. The Elite 100 V2 is the obvious single-input alternative. On paper it matches at 1,000 W and costs $499, but 1,000 W ÷ 20 A means the string must hold at least 50 V while its open-circuit voltage stays at or under 60 V. That is a narrow window, and Notebookcheck's reviewer said 1,000 W is hard to reach in practice. The page should tell shoppers that the two '1,000 W' figures are not equivalent.

findings.label: Lowest string operating voltage that reaches each input's 500 W cap (arithmetic)
findings.source_title: Best Solar Panels for Each Popular Power Station | StormWatts
findings.note: I worked this out from the 15 A and 500 W per-input limits above. Any string operating between 33.3 V and the 60 V Voc ceiling can deliver the full 500 W to each input. At 60 V × 15 A the input could take up to 900 W, so the 500 W cap is what limits it, not the current.

findings.label: Number of solar inputs and connector
findings.value: 1 input, XT connector (12–60 V, max 20 A)
findings.source_title: Good power station or just green marketing? Bio-based Bluetti Elite 100 V2 with 1 kWh reviewed · Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck (Christian Hintze, published 2026-01-06, updated 2026-10-05) writes 'there is only a single solar input' and 'Solar panels (12–60 V, max. 20 A) are connected via an XT connector.' The same review says reaching 1,000 W in practice is difficult and reports no measured solar watts. That last point comes from the fetched summary, not a verbatim quote.

findings.label: Lowest string operating voltage that reaches 1,000 W (arithmetic)
findings.value: 50 V (1,000 W ÷ 20 A), with a 60 V ceiling
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh - BLUETTI US
findings.note: I worked this out from BLUETTI's 12–60 V and 20 A limits. A panel's operating voltage is always below its open-circuit voltage, so a full 1,000 W needs a string that holds 50 V or more under load while its cold Voc stays at or under 60 V. Operating voltage would have to be at least 83% of Voc. DELTA 3 Plus per input: 33.3 V needed out of 60 V (56%). That is the normalisation footnote: same 1,000 W label, very different panel windows.
